---
title: "Introduction"
---
![](./images/adv_r_comm.png){style="width:200px" fig-align="center"}

This is the Website for the NEOF Advance R community analysis workshop.
Unlike our other courses the structure of this course is more flexible as you, the learner, can choose which topics to focus on.

Though this workshop is more flexible there are parts that should be carried out before other parts.

## Prerequisites
![](./images/r_passport.png){style="width:150px" fig-align="center"}

Prior to go through any of this website you should be familiar with the below.
If not, please go through the linked course materials first before continuing on this website.

- Foundations of R
  - Chapters 1 to 11 of the [NEOF R primer for omics](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_j4c0xh/)
- Basic R community analysis with the `phyloseq` and `microbiome` R packages
  - [NEOF R community analysis course](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_community_whqkt8/Course)
- Usage of the `tidyverse` packages `tibble`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `ggplot2`
  - [NEOF Tidyverse cookbook](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/) 
  - [NEOF walkthrough of Tidyverse and the cookbook with learnr tutorials](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/learnr.html)

## Setup
![](/images/setup_4.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 10px" fig-align="center"}

When you are ready to start these materials please start by following the instructions on the [setup page](/setup/setup.qmd).

## Topics

Once you are setup you can choose one of the following five topics to begin.
After finishing one topic you can move onto the next one of your choice.

If you have no particular preference we recommend following the order of this website.
I.e. Rarefaction -> Divergence -> Upset -> MasAsLin3 -> Metadata exploration.

### Rarefaction
![](/rarefaction/images/iterative_rarefaction.png){style="width:200px; border-radius:5px; background:white; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

This part focuses on the alpha and beta diversity analysis with [iterative rarefaction](/rarefaction/rarefaction.qmd).
This explains why and how to use iterations to carry out iterative rarefaction normalisation.
This is much more robust than using one round/iteration of rarefaction.

Additionally, there is a section on [rarefaction slope boxplots](/rarefaction/rareslope_intro.qmd).
This is a new type of rarefaction plot created by me.
This helps you choose which sample to use for rarefaction size/minimum depth filtering.

### Divergence
![](/divergence/images/divergence.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

[Divergence analysis](/divergence/divergence.qmd) is the comparing of dissimilarity distances between (inter-) and within (intra-) groupings. 
This allows us to more closely examine beta diversity.

### Upset
![](/upset/images/upset_plot_icon.png){style="width:300px; background: white; border-radius:15px; border:5px white solid" fig-align="center"}

[Upset plots](/upset/upset.qmd) are a visualisation method to display intersections between sets. 
They can be seen as a different form of a venn diagram but are able to effectively display many intersecting sets.

This part demonstrates how upset plots can be used for community analysis to see:

- What taxa are shared by which samples
- What samples are shared by which taxa

### MaAsLin3
![](/maaslin3/images/maslin.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

[MaAsLin3](/maaslin3/maaslin3.qmd) is a tool to detect feature associations based on metadata groupings using mixed effect models.
It is similar to [`ANCOM-BC2` covered in the R community course](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_community_whqkt8/Course/17-Differential_abundance_analysis.html).
However, MaAsLin3 is a lot more complex but in addition to carrying out abundance association testing it also carried out prevalence association testing.

### Metadata exploration
![](/metadata/images/relative.png){style="border-radius: 15px; width: 200px; background-color: white" fig-align="center"}

[Metadata exploration](/metadata/metadata_exploration.qmd) is very useful you have a lot of metadata variables.
When this is the case it can be difficult to know which variables to use and which to not use, especially for MaAsLin3 analysis.
This part uses correlation analysis to determine which metadata variables are collinear helping with the choice of metadata variables.

This part references a lot of theory presented in the [MaAsLin3 part](/maaslin3/maaslin3.qmd).
We recommend you carry out that part before starting the metadata exploration.
